b35.why: 'He closed the door': Lustig steps away from the shut door, hands calmly behind his back, camera creeps in as the room seals
'spoke quietly... a state secret': leans in toward the seated dealers, one hand shielding his mouth (fallback: warning finger), push closes to whisper distance

b36.why: 'too expensive to maintain': rueful official shrug to the seated dealers as coins drop on the table one after another, the upkeep bill; drift circles the table
'The government has decided': the official decree lands in front of each seated dealer in turn (the document is the point); pull widens to the whole table receiving it
'to demolish it': the real tower alone in the grey, locked frame, a shake and dust as if the wrecking has already begun; the con's core claim made physical

b37.why: 'The public would revolt': imagined Paris reacts, angry reader plus arms-crossed scowl in the rain, small shake on the outrage
'the sale must be kept confidential': back in the salon, hands behind his back beside the shut door; locked-off camera, nothing leaves this room

b38.why: 'A fortune, for the right buyer': raised index finger singles out the one buyer, coin and cash pop in front of the tower as the push lands

b39.why: 'he took them in two limousines': welcoming palm ushers the dealers toward the waiting cars, pan rides along the kerb
'to see the tower in person': the group walks into frame and the camera pans with them until the real tower fills the right

b40.why: 'looking up at it differently... As inventory': one dealer squints up totting up the iron, another rubs his hands, the pull widens to show how much metal there is

x13.why: 'He did not rush them': Lustig waits hands behind back at the edge while a dealer rubs his hands; slow drift, no hurry
'imagine the iron already theirs': greedy smirk fanning cash under the tower; locked frame lets the money sit there as if it were already his

x14.why: 'he has already started to pay for it': the teaching finger states the rule, pull back to the tower he is really selling

b41.why: 'Lustig watched them carefully': hands behind back, still and plotting at the edge of the group; slow drift, the watcher does not move
'he picked his target': hard push lands on one man, a flash marks him as the mark

b42.why: 'without a place in the Parisian elite': Poisson frozen outside the lit grand doors, hat to chest, the pull widens the gap between him and the door

b43.why: 'Poisson wanted to be taken seriously': chest out, lapels gripped, standing tall in the grand salon; slow drift lets him pose
'Lustig gave him exactly that feeling': open palm offered to Poisson like a peer, pan carries the gesture across to him

b44.why: 'He hinted... the highest bidder': a glance over his shoulder to check the room before the contract slides between them; pull gives room to see the two men and the paper
'He thought he was being smart': solo close-up, finger tapping temple with a sly grin, push makes it faintly ridiculous

b45.why: 'Poisson's wife grew suspicious': arms crossed, narrowed eyes on her husband, who freezes with hat clutched and a sweat drop; pan_l follows her stare across to him

b46.why: 'Lustig did not argue': hands calmly behind his back, no fight offered; camera eases back to give him room
'He shifted the story': aha finger up as he turns to face left, the pan swings the frame the other way with the new angle

b47.why: 'He admitted, with embarrassment': eyes down, rubbing his neck, hat in hand; locked frame lets the awkward confession sit
'needs a little extra to survive': helpless shrug of the underpaid official as one coin pops beside him; push on the bribe being asked for

b48.why: 'Poisson relaxed. A bribe made the whole thing feel real': relieved smile, the envelope of cash slides left to the calm, waiting Lustig; pan_l follows the money
'Corruption is something people already believe in': an ordinary doorway, an ordinary man pocketing a tip with a greedy smirk; small corruption as background normal

b49.why: 'believe in a small sin': the teaching finger raised over a single coin, the lesson of the con; push makes the viewer complicit

x15.why: 'Poisson was new to the city's business elite': the newcomer hovers, hat clutched, while an established man stands arms crossed; pan crosses the cold gap

x16.why: 'did not sell him a tower': a shrug beside a toy tower, waving the iron away as beside the point
'He sold him a seat at the table': Lustig's presenting palm ushers Poisson walking past him to the one empty chair at the elite table, contract lands on his place setting as the push closes the act
